paper.title: Online Learning with an Unknown Fairness Metric

settings.name_in_paper: Known objective case (linear contextual bandit with unknown Mahalanobis fairness metric, theta known)
unmapped: The linear reward parameter theta is known to the learner
Learner plays a distribution pi^t and must satisfy individual (Lipschitz) fairness |pi_i - pi_j| <= d(x_i,x_j) for an unknown Mahalanobis distance d(x1,x2)=||Ax1-Ax2||
Fairness oracle feedback: set of pairs on which the fairness constraint was violated
Regret measured against the per-round optimal fair distribution (solution of LP(r_bar, d_bar))
Fairness loss: number of epsilon-unfair pairs summed over rounds
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we consider an easier case of the problem in which the linear objective function $\theta$ is known to the algorithm, and the distance function $d$ is all that is unknown.

settings.name_in_paper: Linear contextual bandit with unknown Mahalanobis fairness metric (full problem)
unmapped: Learner plays a distribution pi^t and must satisfy individual (Lipschitz) fairness |pi_i - pi_j| <= d(x_i,x_j) for an unknown Mahalanobis distance d(x1,x2)=||Ax1-Ax2||
Fairness oracle feedback: set of pairs on which the fairness constraint was violated
Regret measured against the per-round optimal fair distribution (solution of LP(r_bar, d_bar))
Fairness loss: number of epsilon-unfair pairs summed over rounds
settings.definition_quote: An adversary fixes a linear reward function $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $||\theta|| \leq 1$ and a distance function $d$. $\algo$ is given access to the fairness oracle $\cO_d$. In rounds $t = 1$ to $T$: The adversary chooses contexts $x^t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times k}$ with $||x^t_i|| \leq 1$ and gives them to $\algo$. $\algo$ chooses a probability distribution $\pi^t$ over actions, and chooses action $i^t \sim \pi^t$. $\algo$ receives reward $r^t_{i^t}$ and observes feedback $\cO_d(\pi^t)$ from the fairness oracle.

settings.name_in_paper: Generalization to multiple actions per round (fair linear contextual bandit)
unmapped: Learner may pull any subset of the k arms each round, each arm with probability p_i in [0,1]
Individual fairness constraint w.r.t. unknown Mahalanobis distance, fairness oracle feedback
Regret against best fair policy defined by LP_m
settings.definition_quote: In our framework, this corresponds to letting the algorithm take as many as $k$ actions on a single day.

symbols.G_F: Frobenius norm ||A^T A||_F of the Mahalanobis matrix

tuning: Distance estimators instantiated with accuracy epsilon^2

source.label: fairloss
source.quote: For any sequence of contexts and any Mahalanobis distance $d(x_1,x_2) = ||Ax_1-Ax_2||_2$: $$\mathbf{FairnessLoss}(\algo_{\textrm{known}-\theta}, T, \epsilon) \leq   O\left(k^2d^2 \log\left(\frac{d \cdot ||A^TA||_F }{\epsilon}\right)\right)$$

results.notes: Bound on epsilon-fairness loss (number of epsilon-unfair pairs over all rounds), holds with probability 1.

source.label: thm:known-regret
source.quote: For any time horizon $T$: $$ \mathbf{Regret}(\algo_{\textrm{known}-\theta},T) \le O\left(k^2d^2 \log\left(\frac{d \cdot ||A^\top A||_F }{\epsilon}\right) + k^3\epsilon T\right) $$ Setting $\epsilon = O(1/(k^3 T))$ yields a regret bound of $O(d^2\log(||A^\top A||_F\cdot dkT))$.

results.notes: Regret is against the per-round optimal fair distribution, computed with expected rewards; holds for every history. Comparator mapped to best_policy (best fair policy).

source.label: thm:known-regret
source.quote: Setting $\epsilon = O(1/(k^3 T))$ yields a regret bound of $O(d^2\log(||A^\top A||_F\cdot dkT))$.

results.notes: Recorded as stated; the k^2 factor appearing in the general bound is dropped in the paper's tuned statement (likely a typo).

source.label: thm:lastregret
source.quote: For any time horizon $T$, with probability $1-\delta$: $$\mathbf{Regret}(\algo_{full},T) \leq O\left(k^2d^2 \log\left(\frac{d \cdot ||A^\top A||_F }{\epsilon}\right) + k^3\epsilon T + d\sqrt{T}\log(\frac{T}{\delta})\right)$$

results.notes: Regret against best fair policy (per-round LP optimum).

source.label: thm:lastregret
source.quote: If $\epsilon = 1/{k^3 T}$, this is a regret bound of  $O\left(k^2d^2 \log\left(kdT \cdot ||A^\top A||_F \right) + d\sqrt{T}\log(\frac{T}{\delta})\right)$

results.notes: Tuned version requires T to set epsilon.

source.label: thm:fairfull
source.quote: For any sequence of contexts and any Mahalanobis distance $d(x_1,x_2) = ||Ax_1-Ax_2||_2$: $$\mathbf{FairnessLoss}(\algo_{full}, T, \epsilon) \leq   O\left(k^2d^2 \log\left(\frac{d \cdot ||A^\top A||_F }{\epsilon}\right)\right)$$

results.notes: Epsilon-fairness loss bound, holds with probability 1. Appendix states the same bound for the multiple-action variant.
Theorem statement does not explicitly say 'with probability 1-delta' but the proof uses high-probability arguments and delta appears in the bound.
